finding.claim: purge() discards the result of checkPerm(u, "admin"), so the admin permission check is never enforced and purgeAll() runs for any user in context.
finding.source: Authenticated caller's identity via userFrom(r) (handlers.go:25); caller needs only a valid session, no admin permission.
finding.guards_checked: checkPerm is a plain map lookup but its return is discarded; rotateKeys in same file uses mustPerm correctly; route registration and auth middleware are not in the repo, so reachability is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none in purge() (handlers.go:24-29). checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns a bool that line 26 discards, so it has no effect. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) would have enforced the check but is not called, unlike rotateKeys (handlers.go:33). Route registration and auth middleware are not in the repo, so no gate outside this function can be confirmed.
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement and ignores its bool result, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user whose request context carries a *User (userFrom, handlers.go:25); the only remaining uncertainty is whether out-of-repo route middleware restricts the endpoint to admins, which the code here does not show.
